citation: Saint Mary's Church — wood engraving in Andreas's History of Chicago, volume 1 (1884), page 291. Moss Engraving Co., New York; Chicago publisher A. T. Andreas.
author: Moss Engraving Co., New York (engraver); A. T. Andreas (publisher)
date: 1884 (verified publication); date of any earlier drawing or prototype unestablished
describes_date: Undated appearance of the first wooden St Mary's with an open belfry and cross. The original caption gives no year. The repository filename ending 1843 is not a date printed on the engraving. A similar long, low frame church with small steeple, bell and cross is described in Quarter's May 1844 diary, but the engraving is not thereby dated 1844 or proved to depict a particular relocation.
repository: Internet Archive, History of Chicago vol.1, item historyofchicago 01 andr; repository image is a Chicagology reproduction of the same published engraving.
locator: Printed p.291, caption ST. MARY'S CHURCH. Exact published engraving inspected at the archived_url on2026-10-23; its image layout, blank near gable, five tall sash and far-end door on the long wall, open belfry, cross and figures match the held reproduction. Printed p.290 at /page/n600_large.jpg supplies the adjacent historical account; it is textual evidence, cited separately as andreas_1884_v1.
rights_note: Exact engraving located in the 1884 US publication, not inferred solely from the modern reproduction's label. The 1884 printed illustration is public domain in the United States; no modern editorial text is reused as an asset.
what_it_supplies: Visible form: one long low clapboard range, blank near gable, five tall sash and a door at the far end of the visible long wall; open belfry with curved braces, crossed lower railing, curved pointed cap and cross; one chimney toward the far roof end; boarded sidewalk.
A specific 1884 printed-publication provenance and caption for the held picture.
what_it_does_not_supply: No depicted year, relocation site, scale, measured dimensions or surveyed coordinate.
No evidence that the 1835 church lacked a tower or had this precise belfry. Andreas's text dates the initial no-tower state to construction in 1833 and the addition only to some time afterwards.
No secure proof that the picture shows the post-removal enlargement; assigning it to the 1844 textual state is a declared reconstruction, not a captioned date.
access_notes: Whole page and held reference inspected directly. Internet Archive's image URL index and scandata leaf labels disagree in this item; cite the verified printed page and working image URL, not an unverified index calculation.
